newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOXING-POINTS WIN ALLOWS CHOI TO RETAIN WBA LIGHTWEIGHT CROWN.
newsitem.headline: BOXING-POINTS WIN ALLOWS CHOI TO RETAIN WBA LIGHTWEIGHT CROWN.

text.p: Choi Yong-soo of South Korea enjoyed an easy victory over eighth-ranked challenger Yamato Mitani of Japan on Sunday to retain his World Boxing Association (WBA) junior lightweight crown with a unanimous points verdict.
Choi, making his third title defence, took control of the fight in the late rounds.

The win was the 21st of Choi's career, against only two losses. It was his third defeat of Mitani, whom he beat in January in his first title fight after taking the belt in October 1995 with a technical knock-out against Victor Hugo Paz of Argentina.
Mitani, a southpaw sporting blondish-tinted hair, is now 8-3.
Mitani's legs looked rubbery in the late rounds but he stayed on his feet until there were only 17 seconds remaining in the final round.
But after being knocked down the challenger struggled up again before the final bell to deny Choi a knock-out victory.
